issue_context.title: Delete Avatar Problem
issue_context.body:
There is a problem something like this, reproduce:

1. Create 2 organizations
2. Set their avatars as **same** image
3. Delete one organization

Then you will see other organization's avatar reset to default gitea avatar, becouse image removed from disk.

This is same:

- Organization avatar
- User avatar
- Repository avatar

My opinions for solution:

1. Check if there are other same avatar name before remote from disk
2. Check if there are other same avatar name before set avatar and give new name if there
comments: The filename is a hash of the avatar contents. For this, I think we should add the owner as part of the hash and force the names to be different. Otherwise, we'll have to keep a reference count for every file.
IMHO First one does not affect? If a user add same image to multiple organization then remove one

If your NASA organization adds `planet.png` as avatar, the file is uploaded as:
```
data/attachments/e/4/e4dc1049-68cd-4ed0-9636-41c0a04b0a69
```
The name is calculated by hashing its content. If ESA adds the _same_ picture of a planet (no matter the file name, only the byte-by-byte content of the file), then it will be named again:
```
data/attachments/e/4/e4dc1049-68cd-4ed0-9636-41c0a04b0a69
```
That's why if ESA deletes its file, NASA's file gets deleted too. However, if we apply other metadata to the hash input, the hash will be different each case, for example:
```
NASA's planet.png       fe5156a4-6562-49a6-8732-1dbb48639560
ESA's planet.png        b519f855-1e11-4893-b64e-95ca221758cd
```
Even if they are the same file.

That should solve the problem, because if ESA deletes or changes its avatar, only `b519f855-1e11-4893-b64e-95ca221758cd` will be deleted, while `fe5156a4-6562-49a6-8732-1dbb48639560` will remain untouched.

Different user can be add same image but its low probability. Instead, same user can use same image in multi time.
So what will happen if user add same image to organizations and remove one organization?
Or add same image for own avatar and own repos' avatars then delete one repo?

> Different user can be add same image but its low probability. Instead, same user can use same image in multi time.

We are using hash value of the user uploaded image prefixed with userID. So, if same user uploads same photo multiple time as his avatar, it will generate same hash value throughout the time. As we are prefixing the hash value with user id, the avatar name will be always same for same photo & same user.

> So what will happen if user add same image to organizations and remove one organization?

As I mentioned we are prefixing user id with the photo hash, it will not cause any problem. Organization is also like a user having different id. Every organization has different id, so it will not replace the previous image or delete other organization's avatar while deleting another organization.

> Or add same image for own avatar and own repos' avatars then delete one repo?

Repos' avatars are stored in separate directory and also they are prefixing with repo id with image hash which will not conflict with one another.
Even if both avatars are stored in same directory, they will not collide as for user avatar we are taking another hash value of `<hash>[<userid>-<image_hash>]` and for repo the final hash isn't using.

Hope I made myself clear.

What if there is a failure half-way through this migration and so you rerun it?

It looks like in that case you will delete all of the previously migrated newAvatars?

Shouldn't you be testing that the oldAvatar != newAvatar?
